newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money steady, government demand seen.
newsitem.headline: German call money steady, government demand seen.

text.p: German call money rates remained broadly steady on Monday, trading between 3.05 and 3.08 percent in a becalmed market.
Traders said government demand was noticeable in early trade, but had failed to push rates above 3.08 percent level.

After M3 money supply data for March came in very much as expected, suggesting the interest rate background will remain stable for the coming months, players said they expected call money rate to follow suit in the next few sessions.
March M3 growth slowed to an annualised, seasonally -adjusted rate of 8.3 percent versus 9.1 percent in February.
Banks held 40 billion marks in reserve at the Bundesbank on Friday, tightening liquidity slightly from Thursday's session when 40.2 billion marks were held.
The average for the month also dropped slightly, dipping to 40.9 billion marks up until Sunday from 41.1 on Thursday.
Borrowing on the Lombard rate was negligible.
FIONA, the Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Abverage, was quoted at 3.10067 on Monday, marginally tighter than its 3.09933 percent level on Friday.
